messages.author: 89e767987c9b8395
messages.subject: PCA Plot Modification
parts:
Hi,

I'm using methylKit to generate a PCA analysis for 12 samples I have. I've generated the plot, but for publication purposes I need the symbols/labels to be larger and more easily visible. Right now, the text of the samples clustering close to one another overlap, making the plot difficult to read. 

Is there any way to modify the plot that is generated so I can make the area of the plot larger/increase the font of the labels?

Thanks,

Nishanth

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] PCA Plot Modification
parts:
Hi,
You can modify that in image processing software such as Adobe Illustrator.

Another way is to  set obj.return=TRUE
Then, the function returns the result of the prcomp() function on methylation matrix, and you can re-plot with proper formatting.

Best,
Altuna

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Re: PCA Plot Modification
parts:
thanks

I do get different outcomes depending on whether or not I use the obj.return = TRUE.  Did you use any other options that make the PC1, and PC2 proportion variance so different depending on which method below I use...What is the reason why they are so different. 
Sorry I am not very knowledgeable about PCA but I would like to understand the variability in the replicates/samples I have. 

method1

pca.obj = PCASamples(meth10x, screeplot=FALSE,obj.return=TRUE)
summary(pca.obj)
Importance of components:
                            PC1      PC2      PC3      PC4      PC5       PC6       PC7       PC8      PC9
Standard deviation     292.0482 286.1315 265.1404 255.9370 247.0288 109.14962 105.71548 103.79946 103.6581
Proportion of Variance   0.1754   0.1684   0.1446   0.1348   0.1255   0.02451   0.02299   0.02216   0.0221
Cumulative Proportion    0.1754   0.3439   0.4885   0.6232   0.7488   0.77327   0.79626   0.81842   0.8405

method2

mat=percMethylation(meth10x)
prin_comp <- prcomp(mat)
> summary(prin_comp)
Importance of components:
                            PC1      PC2      PC3      PC4      PC5      PC6     PC7     PC8     PC9    PC10
Standard deviation     149.1491 16.90877 16.31485 15.10280 14.56126 13.95166 4.56754 4.46182 4.37484 4.36730
Proportion of Variance   0.9407  0.01209  0.01126  0.00965  0.00897  0.00823 0.00088 0.00084 0.00081 0.00081
Cumulative Proportion    0.9407  0.95282  0.96407  0.97372  0.98268  0.99092 0.99180 0.99264 0.99345 0.99426
On Monday, November 20, 2017 at 5:37:26 AM UTC-5, Altuna Akalin wrote:

https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/methylKit/versions/0.99.2/topics/percMethylation can get you the matrix for PCA. 

But PCASamples can return the object returned by prcomp function, if you provide obj.return=TRUE. check the documentation for the function. then check the documentation for prcomp function to figure out % variation explained by components
On Sun, Nov 19, 2017 at 4:11 AM, Linda Molla <molla...@gmail.com> wrote:

Also regarding the function PCASamples(meth, screeplot=TRUE)
How can I figure out what are the values of the x-axis ( I want to know which elements provide the most variability). 

thanks,
Linda
On Saturday, November 18, 2017 at 9:58:08 PM UTC-5, Linda Molla wrote:

I am interested in knowing what the % variance is in the PCA plot coordinates. I would like to generate the PCA using the prcomp function. 
Is there a way to extract the matrix used for the PCA ( after generating the unite function).  If not any tips on generating it?
On Thursday, November 16, 2017 at 6:19:05 AM UTC-5, Altuna Akalin wrote:
PC1 should explain the most variance.
On Thu, Nov 16, 2017 at 12:57 AM, Linda Molla <molla...@gmail.com> wrote:
I have a question that is related a bit, regarding the PCA plots. How does PC1 compare to PC2. Which is the one that explains most of the variance??

Thank,
Linda
On Monday, September 4, 2017 at 2:02:10 AM UTC-4, Altuna Akalin wrote:

Hi Sol,
It probably doesn't work for all the plots. But most of them are straightforward. You can see the function source code to understand how plots are produced and make custom plotting functions based on the original plotting functions. 

Best,
Altuna
On Mon, Sep 4, 2017 at 1:15 AM, Sunny Sun <sols...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Altuna,

Thank you, I used this option for the PCA plot and it works nicely, does it work for all the plots? I would like to customize them all for style consistency.

Thanks
Sol
2017-09-02 12:03 GMT+02:00 Altuna Akalin <aak...@gmail.com>:
As I described above, you can get the data used for the scatter plot using the following argument in the function
obj.return=TRUE
On Sat, 2 Sep 2017 at 06:36, <sols...@gmail.com> wrote:

In some plots the name of the samples go outside the margins of the plots and i can't see them. How do you obtain the data to use for customized plots, for example if I want to use ggplot?


On Wednesday, July 19, 2017 at 4:42:31 AM UTC+2, solo...@gmail.com wrote:
Hi,

I'm using methylKit to generate a PCA analysis for 12 samples I have. I've generated the plot, but for publication purposes I need the symbols/labels to be larger and more easily visible. Right now, the text of the samples clustering close to one another overlap, making the plot difficult to read. 

Is there any way to modify the plot that is generated so I can make the area of the plot larger/increase the font of the labels?

Thanks,

Nishanth
